name: manual_c4e03e
claim: A whole-file git conflict (markers spanning nearly the entire file) usually means one side substantially rewrote the file while the other commit never intended to touch it at all — check 'git show <incoming-commit> -- <file>' first; if the incoming commit's own diff is empty for that file, its tree snapshot is just stale carry-through, and the correct resolution is almost always --ours (the side with the real, intentional changes), not a line-by-line merge.
conditions: whole file conflict git show incoming commit stale carry-through ours theirs rebase

decisions.notes: 2026-07-03: scripts/spawn_agents.py conflicted from line 1 to EOF during a rebase. Verified via 'git show c31741c -- scripts/spawn_agents.py' that the incoming lm-link commit made zero changes to that file; upstream's 57a8a57 series was a genuine 727-line dispatch-race rewrite. Taking --ours avoided silently reverting real work.
